messages:
matt: FYI infra-ci is flaking on gpu-provision branch — helm upgrade for model-serving canary is timing out and leftover runner jobs are queuing.
ci-bot: workflow infra-deploy (run #342) failed: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/actions/runs/342 — error: helm upgrade --install timed out after 600s
julia: log snippet? can you paste the failing step output
matt: ```
Installing chart/model-serving...
Error: UPGRADE FAILED: timed out waiting for the condition
helm error: rpc timeout, waiting for rollout
actions/cache: restore failed with status 403 for key: gha-infra-cache-v1
Runner queue length: 14, concurrency=4
```
ashley: Hmm 403 on cache restore + high runner queue — smells like cache throttling + runner contention while nodepool rotate was happening earlier.
kevin: Did node rotation coincide with the run? we had a scheduled gke nodepool rotation at 03:10 UTC today.
matt: yes rotation started ~03:08 UTC and autoscaler briefly rebalanced pods. Some preemptions observed, pods evicted -> helm waited for pods to be ready.
infra-oncall: I saw the same in cluster logs: several GPU nodes in pool rebooted for kernel patch; kubelet re-registered after ~4m. Also saw GCP API rate limiting on instance group updates.
julia: Short term mitigation ideas?
kevin: Options: 1) force helm timeout longer (+retry wrapper), 2) reduce GH Actions concurrency on infra repo to 1 for deploy jobs so we don't thundering herd on scarce GPU nodes, 3) pin deploys to dedicated runner group that isn't autoscaled/preemptible.
matt: Tried rerun with cache bypass (actions/cache disabled) and concurrency set to 1 — run succeeded after 2 retries (helm completed). So cache 403 definitely contributed to stall.
ashley: I'll open a small PR to add a retry loop around helm upgrade and to set `concurrency: 1` for the deploy job. Also adding `--atomic --timeout 10m` to helm args.
matt: PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/778 — contains job changes + fallback step to skip canary if cluster health < 80% (simple kubectl check)
kevin: Long term: consider an "infra-deploy" runner pool on non-preemptible GPUs or a tiny dedicated control-plane pool to handle deploy orchestration. Yes costy but prevents outages.
julia: Agree; cost estimate? if we keep 1x nvidia-t4 on-demand for control-plane pool ~0.25 GPU-hours/day => ~7.5 GPU-hours/month; rough infra cost delta ~ $300-500/mo depending on region.
infra-oncall: I'll schedule a 2h experiment: spin up a small dedicated pool in us-west1 and route infra-deploy jobs there for next 48h. Monitoring on this thread.
ci-bot: rerun triggered by matt: infra-deploy #342 -> run #343
matt: run #343 shows helm succeeded after ~7m when routed to dedicated runner (bypassed cache). Looks stable so far.
ashley: Going to land PR with retry + concurrency change, and a follow-up issue to evaluate dedicated pool. Will also add a cache restore backoff (exponential) to reduce 403 storms.
kevin: Also add a guard: if helm fails 3 times in a row on canary, auto-pause canary rollout and create a ticket in #incidents for manual review.
julia: Sounds good. Thanks for the quick triage everyone. :thumbsup:
infra-oncall: Monitoring alerts set: if deploy failure rate > 20% over 1h, auto-mute canary rollouts and notify infra-oncall.
matt: I'll merge the PR after CI passes and keep an eye on next 6 deploys.
ashley: merged and rolled out. will post a follow-up metrics snapshot tomorrow.
kevin: nice work. :rocket:
